plan.structureSummary: The rule takes the intersection of the player’s ticket list and the draw list, then reduces that intersection by counting its elements. It compares the resulting count with the constant 3 using a greater‑than‑or‑equal predicate. The player wins if the count is at least three.

runs.proposal: The player wins if the sum of the six guessed numbers is greater than the sum of the six drawn numbers.

plan.structureSummary: The decision tree first takes each raw list (the player's ticket and the draw) and applies a reduce operation to compute the sum of its six numbers. Those two sums are then fed into a compare predicate that checks whether the ticket sum is greater than the draw sum. The rule evaluates to true (the player wins) when that comparison holds.

plan.structureSummary: The rule computes the intersection of the guessed ticket list and the draw list, counts how many numbers are in that intersection, and checks that this count equals exactly two. If the equality holds, the ticket is a winner; otherwise it is not.

plan.structureSummary: The rule takes the ticket list, reduces it by summing all six numbers, computes the remainder of that sum when divided by 2, and compares the remainder to 0. The player wins when the remainder is 0 (i.e., the sum is even).

runs.proposal: The player wins if at least four of the six guessed numbers are odd.

plan.structureSummary: The tree starts with the ticket list (source). It filters the list, keeping only numbers whose remainder when divided by 2 is non‑zero (odd). The filtered list is reduced with a count operation to obtain the number of odd entries. Finally a compare predicate checks whether that count is at least 4.

runs.proposal: The player wins if the difference between the highest and lowest guessed number is less than 30.

plan.structureSummary: The tree begins with the source list of guessed numbers. Two reduce nodes compute the maximum and minimum of that list, an arithmetic node subtracts the minimum from the maximum, and a compare node checks whether that difference is less than the constant 30. The rule returns true (the player wins) when the comparison succeeds.

runs.proposal: O jogador ganha somente se acertar pelo menos dois números e a soma do seu jogo for maior que a soma do sorteio.

plan.structureSummary: The tree first takes the two raw number lists (the ticket and the draw) as sources. It computes the intersection of the two lists and reduces it by count to get the number of matches, and also reduces each list by sum to get their total values. It then compares the match count to the constant 2 and the ticket sum to the draw sum, finally combining the two comparisons with an AND predicate.

plan.structureSummary: First, take the guessed ticket list and replace each number with its unit digit, then drop duplicates and count the remaining values. Do the same for the drawn list. Finally, compare the two counts and win if the guessed count is greater.

runs.proposal: Among all submitted tickets, the ticket matching the greatest number of drawn numbers wins. Tied tickets all win and share the prize.

plan.structureSummary: For each submitted ticket the rule forms the intersection of the ticket’s six numbers with the six drawn numbers, then reduces that intersection by counting its elements. The count is the ticket’s score. Tickets are ranked by these scores, and any ticket(s) with the highest count win (ties are allowed).

runs.proposal: O jogador ganha se exatamente uma destas condições for verdadeira: acertou exatamente três números; ou a soma do jogo é igual à soma do sorteio.

plan.structureSummary: The rule first computes the size of the intersection of the ticket and the draw and checks whether it equals three. Separately it computes the sum of the ticket and the sum of the draw and checks for equality. The final win condition is true when exactly one of these two sub‑conditions holds, which can be expressed as (cond1 AND NOT cond2) OR (cond2 AND NOT cond1).

runs.proposal: Only tickets matching at least two drawn numbers are eligible. Among eligible tickets, the ticket with the smallest difference between its highest and lowest number wins; all ties win and share the prize.

plan.structureSummary: First the rule computes the intersection of a ticket’s numbers with the draw and counts how many match; only tickets with a count of at least two pass a filter. For each surviving ticket it reduces the ticket list to its range span (highest minus lowest) and the ticket(s) with the smallest span win, with ties shared.

runs.proposal: Separe os números do jogo entre acertados e não acertados. O jogador ganha se algum número não acertado tiver o mesmo algarismo das unidades que algum número acertado.

plan.structureSummary: The rule first separates the ticket numbers into correct (intersection of ticket and draw) and incorrect (difference of ticket and draw). Both groups are transformed to their unit‑digit values, intersected, and the ticket wins if this intersection is non‑empty (i.e., at least one unit digit appears in both groups).

runs.proposal: Keep both sequences in their stated order and compare them in mirror order: first guess to last draw, second guess to fifth draw, and so on. The player wins if at least one mirrored pair contains the same number.

plan.structureSummary: First the draw list is reversed to obtain the mirrored order. The ticket list (source) and the reversed draw list are then examined pair‑wise using a pairs_exists predicate that checks each position pair with a compare predicate for equality. The rule succeeds (the player wins) if any mirrored pair contains the same number.

plan.structureSummary: The tree first reduces each ticket and the draw to their total sums and keeps only tickets whose sum is less than the draw's sum. For each surviving ticket it maps every number to its unit digit, removes duplicates, counts the remaining distinct unit digits, and uses that count as the ticket's score for ranking; the highest score wins, ties split the prize.

runs.proposal: The player wins only when exactly one of these three statements is true: at least three guessed numbers were drawn; the guessed numbers sum to more than the drawn numbers; the player's highest number was drawn.

plan.structureSummary: The tree first builds the intersection of the ticket and the draw and uses a reduction to count how many guessed numbers appear, checking that this count is at least three. It also reduces both lists to their sums and compares the ticket sum to the draw sum, and reduces the ticket to its maximum value and tests whether that value is contained in the draw. Finally the three Boolean results are combined with logical and, or and not to enforce that exactly one of them is true, yielding the win/lose outcome.
